summary: Renewal check-in focused on latency-sensitive workloads. Customer evaluating 2x capacity uplift + EU region addition and contract extension for 12 months. Main asks: concrete p95/p99 latencies under sample traffic, VPC/private deployment notes, and a short amendment for billing and commitment. Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmark, security docs, legal sync.
topics: contract amendment / term and billing cadence
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood. Diego and Priya are with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Nate (AstraCore): Hey Maya, good, thanks. Morning for some of us.
[00:12] Elena (AstraCore): Afternoon, sorry we're juggling an oncall.
[00:18] Diego (Redwood SE): No worries, we'll keep it tight. Today's goal is to align on capacity uplift, EU region add, and what you need for the renewal amendment.
[00:30] Marta (AstraCore): Yeah, main thing is our latency tail — p95 spikes when we hit batch reporting windows. We're trying to avoid moving everything onprem.
[00:40] Priya (Redwood): Understood. Quick question on current traffic shape — Nate, is your 95th percentile dominated by background batch requests or user interactive bursts?
[00:48] Nate: It's a mix. The interactive front-end has spikes and then our reconciliation jobs hit the same model endpoints. It's causing locked KV cache misses and then latency climbing.
[00:58] Diego: When you say KV cache misses, do you mean prefix cache invalidations or warm/cold KV evictions?
[01:05] Nate: Sorry, yeah, K-V cash — evictions. We see the cache TTL drop during big jobs.
[01:11] Elena: And we're running a multi-tenant VPC today with our cloud provider.
[01:16] Maya: Cool. For the uplift you're asking about — you mentioned 2x capacity?
[01:20] Marta: We want headroom for next quarter. If we can guarantee p95 below 220ms for the interactive path, we'll be comfortable. p99 is less critical but would be great under 600ms.
[01:34] Diego: Ok, that's a clear SLO. Two comments: 1) host type matters — Dedicated pools can give much tighter p95 because of stable batching behavior; 2) routing and prefix caching reduce tokens and improve tail.
[01:50] Jamie? (background) Speaker 3: [inaudible]...
[01:55] Maya: (laughs) Ignore the phantom speaker. So on pricing — do you want monthly committed or quarterly?
[02:02] Jamal (AstraCore): Procurement leaning toward quarterly to keep flexibility, but finance wants predictability for the next 12 month term. We might do an initial 6-month commit with option to extend.
[02:14] Priya: That's common. We can draft an amendment that has a 6-month firm commit and an appending optional renewal for another 6 months at pre-agreed uplift rates.
[02:25] Marta: Legal will want to see data residency for EU region and KMS integration.
[02:31] Maya: We'll include KMS/HSM notes — Priya will send the VPC onboarding checklist and SOC2/ISO summary. Our private deployment option can be behind a customer-managed VPC if you need tighter residency.
[02:44] Nate: Quick technical: if we add EU region, what's the impact on routing and cross-region cache coherence?
[02:51] Diego: Good question. We typically route users regionally. Cross-region cache coherence isn't automatic; you get separate KV caches per region which helps latency but can increase token generation cost due to missed prefixes on cold starts. There's a tradeoff: lower latency vs higher cost and warmup.
[03:08] Elena: Could we use prefix warmers or a pre-warm window around batch jobs?
[03:12] Diego: Yes, we can schedule warmers and cache seeding to avoid cold tails. We'll show a plan in the benchmark.
[03:18] Maya: Let's talk benchmarks — Diego, can you outline what you'll run?
[03:22] Diego: I'll use AstraCore's sample trace you shared, run a steady-state interactive mix and a bursty reconciliation mix. Collect p50/p95/p99, median generation tokens, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens. I want to show Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) for EU+US.
[03:40] Nate: How long will that take?
[03:42] Diego: For a meaningful tail, 48 hours gives a decent p99 picture. We can do an initial 6-hour smoke test and share preliminary numbers within 48 hours.
[03:50] Marta: That works. One ask — please include sampling of quantized model variants in the run; we may accept slight quality tradeoffs for latency.
[03:58] Diego: Will do. We'll include int8 quantized variants and a 16-bit baseline.
[04:03] Elena: On security, two things: audit logs retention and KMS key rotation.
[04:08] Priya: Redwood supports audit logs to your SIEM and configurable retention; KMS integration supports both bring-your-own (BYOK) and Redwood-managed keys. I'll attach the KB link.
[04:19] Jamal: Also need billing alignment — do you meter per-token with a minimum monthly commitment?
[04:24] Maya: Yes, hosted is per-token with tiered discounts for commits. Dedicated is a capacity reservation model with monthly invoicing. For the amendment, we can offer a blended rate for the first six months.
[04:36] Nate: Any examples from other fintech customers around SLO language for latency?
[04:41] Maya: We typically propose operational SLOs in the contract appendix — example: p95 < 220ms for interactive endpoints with agreed traffic shape and a penalty-free investigation window. We can share anonymized examples.
[04:54] Elena: Sounds good. Back to architecture — if we move some reconciliation jobs to a different model variant with lower token footprint, do you support routing rules at request-time?
[05:03] Diego: Yes, Smart routing can send requests based on policy. You could route reconciliation to a cheaper quantized model and interactive to the higher-quality baseline.
[05:11] Marta: I like that. The trick is validating quality on the cheaper model.
[05:15] Diego: We'll run A/B checks and can attach a small eval harness to the benchmark to track quality metrics.
[05:22] Maya: Let's cover timelines. You said procurement wants a draft by mid-March?
[05:27] Jamal: Preferably the 11th for a legal sync, that leaves time for approvals.
[05:31] Maya: Ok, we'll target draft amendment 2026-03-11.
[05:34] [06:00] Speaker 2 (customer): Quick question about failover — if EU region has an outage, do we fail to US and what are latency implications?
[06:10] Priya: You can set automated failover policies. In practice, failing over to a different region will increase latency for EU users; we can provide metrics from past incidents to help you model user impact.
[06:22] Nate: Do you support data residency controls so that failed-over requests don't write sensitive logs in a secondary region?
[06:29] Diego: We can redact or route logs to your primary region; also discuss with security team on cross-region audit logs. We'll document options.
[06:38] Marta: On pricing detail — can you show cost per 1M tokens for each model + region?
[06:44] Maya: We'll include a pricing matrix in the spreadsheet. It will show hosted token rate, dedicated effective token cost given commit, and private deployment one-time/setup fees.
[06:54] Elena: Are there constraints on model versions for Private (on-prem) deployments?
[06:59] Priya: Private can run most curated models; some bleeding-edge kernels require specific hardware. We'll list compatibility.
[07:07] Diego: Also note quantized kernels vary by hardware; int8 perf on A100 + custom kernels is different than on older GPUs.
[07:16] Nate: We're on a tight calendar — if benchmarks are good, leadership will likely greenlight the 6-month commit. If not, we may negotiate a smaller bump.
[07:26] Maya: Understood. Anything else on the technical front?
[07:29] Marta: One more: tracing integration. We want request-level IDs traced into our observability.
[07:34] Priya: Redwood has tracing hooks and per-request metadata; we can push into your Jaeger/Datadog pipeline. I'll attach the integration snippet.
[07:43] Jamal: For procurement, can we get a sample invoice for a hypothetical 2x uplift?
[07:48] Maya: Yes, we'll include a sample invoice in the pricing pack.
[07:52] [15:00] (longer silence while notes are recorded and Diego screenshares a plan)
[15:20] Diego: I'm sharing the benchmark plan doc in chat (link: drive.redwood/benchmark-plan) — it has scenarios, metrics, and a data schema we need.
[15:30] Elena: Got it. We'll drop the sample trace and traffic matrix by EOD.
[15:36] Nate: We'll also include the current p95/p99 numbers from our monitoring so you can correlate.
[15:41] Diego: Perfect. We'll do an initial 6-hour soak and then run the 48-hour tail run.
[15:48] Marta: On the amendment language — we want the flexibility to shift 20% of committed capacity between regions in a given month. Is that allowed?
[15:56] Maya: We can add a flexibility clause for region reallocation up to a threshold per billing period. We'll confirm with Ops and legal.
[16:05] Jamal: Also include a clause on data deletion and end-of-term data handling.
[16:10] Priya: Standard stuff — at termination we provide a data export and guarantee deletion within X days. We'll include specifics.
[16:17] [23:00] Diego: One potential optimization — use hybrid routing where high-priority interactive requests go to dedicated GPUs while low-priority batch jobs hit burst capacity. It reduces cost while preserving SLOs.
[23:12] Marta: That seems promising. How do we manage throttling during big reconciles?
[23:18] Diego: You can use request tiering and graceful degradation; Redwood supports automatic fallback to cheaper model or queueing with estimated time.
[23:28] Nate: Any performance regressions we should watch for when enabling quantization?
[23:33] Diego: Small ones in semantic similarity in corner cases; we'll measure evals.
[23:38] Elena: Does your console surface token-level cost per route?
[23:42] Maya: Yes, per-route cost and token breakdowns and there's tracing per model. We'll add screenshots in the deck.
[23:50] [30:00] (quick recap) Maya: Recap — Diego runs benchmarks (6-hour smoke then 48‑hour tail); Priya sends security + VPC docs; Maya sends pricing matrix and sample invoice; legal sync on 2026-03-11. Any objections?
[30:12] Jamal: No objections. Procurement will review pricing but timeline is tight.
[30:17] Marta: Quality metrics are important — include A/B eval harness.
[30:21] Diego: Will include.
[30:24] Elena: Also include a short runbook for failovers in the docs.
[30:28] Priya: Noted.
[30:31] Nate: One more thing — can we trial the EU region with a small pilot before full region flip? Maybe 10% of interactive traffic?
[30:38] Maya: Yes, a canary/pilot is the standard approach. We'll propose a rollout plan with thresholds.
[30:44] Jamal: That helps procurement mitigate risk.
[30:48] Maya: Great. Anything else?
[30:50] Marta: No, that's it from us.
[30:52] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and the dates.
[30:57] Diego: I'll start the benchmark once you share traces.
[31:02] [47:30] (meeting ends)
[47:33] Maya: Bye all, thanks.
questions: What are AstraCore's exact p95/p99 SLO targets?
Can Redwood guarantee p95 < 220ms for interactive endpoints under the provided traffic?
What legal flexibility is there for region reallocation within a billing period?
